# Plan: Stuck states P8c — security-dependency holds escalate after `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_ESCALATE_DAYS` and release on an unmerged predecessor

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8291` at `f1e64a0f04e6201cc7f92e36a5c1b9cddfbd6541` (integration branch matches; no mismatch). Refs #8291 (tracking issue — PR body must use `Refs #8291`, never an auto-close keyword).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends security_dependency_verdict
Scope-mode justification: This issue delivers item 3 of P8 in `docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md` ("Extend the security-dependency hold branch"). The work extends three existing pieces: the verdict helper `security_dependency_verdict` in `scripts/security_dependency.py`; the hold branch of `run_standalone_stall_recovery` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (lines 23914-23967); and the existing standalone stall-state comment (`AI_STANDALONE_STALL_STATE_V1`, helpers at lines 18546-18640). It adds no new script, workflow or supervisor. The generic `Depends on: #N` wait and Phases 4a/4b (`dependency_wait_resume.py`, `ai:waiting-on-dependency`) are separate sibling P8 issues and stay out of scope.

Applying the "Boil the Lake" rule (§6 Core Priorities: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the plan adds three things that cost about 30 LOC or less each:
- switch-off parity in the clarify and implement gates;
- removing the escalation latch on release;
- a test case for the wrapper predicate.

Without them, the unmerged-predecessor release would loop, or the issue would stay latched after the dependency resolves.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/security_dependency.py`
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
- `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`
- `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`
- `.github/workflows/implement.yml`
- `tests/test_security_dependency.py`
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py`
- `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py`
- `README.md`
- `agents.d/stuck-states-p8c-security-hold.md` (new)
- `changelog.d/stuck-states-p8c-security-hold.md` (new)

## Automation / scheduler wiring (§20.E)
- **Change type:** only existing code changes. No new script, no new supervisor, no DB work.
- **Entry point:** the existing standalone stall recovery sweep `run_standalone_stall_recovery`. It is called from `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 26641 and 33278, and runs on the cron and dispatch triggers of `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`. The two poller steps that run it take the new env rows next to `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HOLD_MAX_DAYS` (workflow lines 1340 and 1567).
- **Supervisor:** none required. The poller cron already re-checks every held issue on each tick.
- **Removal registry:** no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry, because no new script is introduced.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/security_dependency.py`
- Add a module helper `_dependency_wait_resume_enabled()`. It reads `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED` from `os.environ`, defaulting to `true` in the helper itself (§8: the helper is staged from a git ref, so the default has to live there). `false`, `0`, `no` and `off` (case-insensitive) mean off; any other value means on.
- In `security_dependency_verdict`, when the switch is on and the prerequisite is a readable same-repo issue in state `closed` without `ai:merged`, return `{"status": "ready", "reason": "dependency closed without ai:merged", "depends_on": N}`. The reason string stays exactly as today.
  - With the switch off, return today's `held` verdict unchanged.
  - Every other branch is unchanged. Open dependencies and malformed, mismatched or unreadable prerequisites all stay `held`.
- Update the module docstring: a predecessor closed unmerged is now released, so the follow-up is re-clarified (stuck-states P8c).

**Why the verdict has to change.** clarify (`.github/workflows/clarify.yml:920-923`) and implement (`.github/workflows/implement.yml:2386-2388`, `:2824-2826`) both skip on any `held` status. If only the poller posted a `/reclarify`, clarify would re-hold the issue and the release would loop.

### 2. `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`

**(a) Stall-state normalizer.** `_extract_standalone_state_json_from_comments` (lines 18553-18593) normalizes with jq and drops unknown keys, so the new keys must be added there or they are lost on every read. Add these keys to its jq object:
- `security_dependency_depends_on`
- `security_dependency_held_since_ts`
- `security_dependency_escalated_ts`

Each is parsed with `(try tonumber catch 0)` and defaults to 0. Callers treat a missing key (from the default-state literals) as 0.

**(b) Config parse, once per sweep.** At the top of `run_standalone_stall_recovery`, beside the existing locals (lines 23860-23880):
- `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED`: default `true`. Accept `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`, `yes`, `no`, `on` and `off`; any other value emits `::warning::` and falls back to `true`.
- `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_ESCALATE_DAYS`: default `7`. Must match `^[0-9]{1,4}$` and be at least 1; otherwise emit `::warning::` and use 7.
- Export `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED` so the helper call at line 23932 sees the same value.
- Declare every new local with a unique `_security_dependency_*` prefix (checked: none exist today besides `_security_dependency_issue_file`, `_security_dependency_verdict` and `_security_dependency_status`).

**(c) Held branch, `open` sub-case** (currently lines 23936-23944). Only when the switch is on and the mapped status is `open`, call a new function `_security_dependency_hold_age_check <issue> <depends_on> <comments_json> <labels_json> <cache_available>`, placed beside the stall-state helpers. It does the following:
1. Parse state with `_extract_standalone_state_json_from_comments`.
2. If `security_dependency_held_since_ts` is 0, is in the future, or `security_dependency_depends_on` differs from the verdict's `depends_on`:
   - set `held_since_ts=$(date -u +%s)`, `depends_on=N` and `escalated_ts=0`;
   - write the state once with `write_standalone_state_json`, passing the cached state comment id;
   - log `STALL_SKIP issue=<n> reason=security_dependency_hold_recorded action=none`.
   - **Duplicate-comment guard:** when the comment cache is not `true` or holds 100 or more comments, first do the same bounded paginated comments read the ready path already uses (lines 23948-23952) before writing. Otherwise the write could create a duplicate state comment. If that read fails, log `reason=security_dependency_comments_unavailable` and write nothing.
3. Else, if `now - held_since_ts >= DEPENDENCY_WAIT_ESCALATE_DAYS*86400`, `escalated_ts` is 0, `labels_json` lacks `ai:needs-human`, and the complete comment history (same bounded read) has no trusted latch marker for this `depends_on`, then escalate:
   - `ensure_label_exists 'ai:needs-human'` and add the label, following the pattern at lines 20295-20296.
   - Post one comment ending `<!-- ai:needs-human-latch reason=security_dependency_wait depends_on=<M> -->`. Its text says:
     - the dependency chain `#<n> → #<M> (open)`;
     - the days waited and the UTC ISO `held_since`;
     - that the hold stays in place and releases automatically on merge or on an unmerged close.
     - It contains only integers and fixed text.
   - Set `escalated_ts=now` in the state and write it.
   - Log `STALL_SKIP issue=<n> reason=security_dependency_escalated action=needs_human`.
4. **Trusted markers.** A marker is trusted only when its author login equals `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`, resolved with `unblock_trusted_login` (the pattern the PR-dependency branch uses at line 23983). If the identity cannot be resolved, skip escalation for this tick (`reason=security_dependency_identity_unavailable`).
5. The existing `STALL_SKIP ... reason=security_dependency_held detail=<status>` line and the `continue` stay unchanged.

**(d) Ready branch** (lines 23945-23967). Branch on the verdict reason:
- **`dependency merged`:** today's path, unchanged. Marker `<!-- ai:security-dependency-released:<n> -->`, author_association trust.
- **`dependency closed without ai:merged`:**
  - Resolve `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`. If it is unavailable, log `reason=security_dependency_identity_unavailable` and `continue` (hold kept).
  - Make sure the comment history is complete, using the same bounded read.
  - If no comment by the trusted login starts with `"/reclarify\n<!-- AI_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_RELEASED_V1 reason=predecessor_unmerged"`, post `"/reclarify\n<!-- AI_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_RELEASED_V1 reason=predecessor_unmerged issue=<n> depends_on=<M> -->"`. Log `STALL_SKIP issue=<n> reason=security_dependency_released_unmerged action=reclarify` (or `reason=security_dependency_retrigger_failed`), then `continue`.
  - If the marker already exists, fall through to normal stall recovery, the same as the merged path does today.

**(e) Latch removal on release.** In both release sub-paths, just before posting the `/reclarify`, remove `ai:needs-human` (one idempotent `DELETE issues/<n>/labels/ai:needs-human`, failure logged as `::warning::` and ignored) only when all of these hold:
- `labels_json` has `ai:needs-human`;
- the latest trusted-login comment containing `<!-- ai:needs-human-latch` is the `reason=security_dependency_wait` one.

Log `STALL_SKIP issue=<n> reason=security_dependency_latch_cleared action=none`. Any other latch reason is left alone.

**(f) Clearing hold keys.** In the `updated_state` Python block (lines 24108-24126), which an issue reaches only when it is not held, drop the three `security_dependency_*` keys. The next ordinary state write then clears the hold episode.
